newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish bourse suspends three electrical shares.
newsitem.headline: Spanish bourse suspends three electrical shares.

text.p: The Spanish bourse watchdog CNMV suspended trade in the shares of three electrical groups on Friday, igniting talk state-run Endesa would take over the two regional groups before privatisation.

The CNMV announced the suspension of shares and options in 66-percent state-owned Empresa Nacional de Electricidad (Endesa), Fuerzas Electricas de Catalunya (Fecsa) and Sevillana de Electricidad pending an announcement.
"We are awaiting a decision from the cabinet," a CNMV spokeswoman said.

She gave no further details, but news the cabinet would make a decision on the matter at its regular weekly meeting sparked market talk of Endesa buying a large majority stake in the two via a share offering in the two regional suppliers.
Endesa, a tranche of which will be privatised next year, already holds a 39.4 percent stake in Sevillana and a 49 percent stake in Fecsa.

The success of Endesa's privatisation is uncertain, given worries about the future of the electricity sector and its laws which are now being revised in part to harmonise with European Union legislation.
But analysts speculate that this purchase which would give Endesa, an electric generator, its first distribution network would help compensate it for what are likely to be adverse legal changes.
The CNMV said trade in the shares might resume after a cabinet decision.
